Build only this feature on this page. Get it working, test it, and then move on.

What you are building

Delete one chosen task from JSON storage without damaging the rest of the saved structure. You are rebuilding the same feature with JSON storage, so keep the user experience aligned while the persistence model changes.

The key idea for this feature is Identifier-led deletion and safe document rewrite.. Before you write anything, make sure you can describe what the user should see or what the request should do when this feature is finished.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
IdentifierA stable value used to target the correct record.
Delete actionA request that removes one stored record.
ConfirmationA deliberate check before a destructive action.
Record removalDeleting data cleanly and predictably.

Why this still matters to the client

  • The client still expects one clear record of current work. Delete only works if the correct object is removed safely.
  • This feature is a reminder that flexibility does not remove the need for disciplined updates.

What to carry in from earlier pages

  • Reuse the row-level identifier thinking from the SQL delete lesson.
  • Bring forward the JSON write-safety notes from the backend setup pages.

Delete design habit

Destructive actions should always be tied to a stable identifier. If two tasks have the same title, the title is not safe enough to delete by.

Delete action preview

Delete needs to target one specific record, not whichever line happens to look right.

Prepare report task_id = 8 Delete

How this feature moves through the stack

HTMLJavaScriptFlaskStorageResponse

Useful reference before you code

  • Delete actions must target a stable identifier, not visible text.
  • The interface should make it clear which record is about to be removed.
  • After deletion, the visible list and stored data must agree.

Generic delete-request pattern

function deleteItem(id) {
  return fetch(`/api/items/${id}`, {
    method: "DELETE"
  });
}
id

The identifier must belong to the record, not just to the visual row.

template literal

Backticks let you insert the id into the URL with `${...}`.

DELETE

DELETE tells the backend this request is meant to remove one record.

return

Returning the fetch promise makes it easier to chain a refresh or message afterwards.

Build it in this order

Deleting from JSON usually means rebuilding the list without the chosen record, then saving the new structure.

Step 1 static/js/app.js

Attach the delete action to each rendered row

  • Pass the record id into the delete request rather than relying on title text.
  • Keep the UI action aligned with the SQL version so only the storage logic changes.
Step 2 app.py

Filter out the chosen object and save the remaining list

  • Load the tasks, keep every object except the target, then save the updated list.
  • Explain why this is a rewrite step rather than a single-row delete query.

Ask yourself

  • How can you prove the correct object was removed?
  • Why is the resulting JSON file still part of the feature evidence?

Where the checks happen

HTML

The interface can require fields, constrain control types, and guide the user before submit.

JavaScript

The browser can check presence, shape, and request timing before sending data.

Flask

The backend must re-check the request because outside tools can bypass the browser entirely.

JSON write step

The document write logic must reject or repair bad structures before saving.

Where your work goes

File or areaWhy this file mattersWhat belongs in this feature
static/js/app.jsTriggers the delete request from the right rowPass the task id rather than the title text
app.pyRemoves the chosen object from the stored listLoad, filter, save, and return a clear response
data/tasks.jsonHolds the remaining recordsThe file must still be valid after deletion

When this feature is ready to sign off

  • Delete targets the correct stored record.
  • The saved JSON structure remains valid after the rewrite.
  • The browser redraw confirms the correct row disappeared.
